thread:
marie: Heads-up: running into a weird slow-consumer spike on the Python SSE client when KV-cache warms. Large responses (5-10kb) are getting split mid-JSON and our incremental parser stalls and the consumer queue balloons. Anyone seen this pattern?

ashok: Yep. Seen similar — partial JSON objects split across chunks + no heartbeat = client stalls. Do you have a tiny repro?

marie: Short log excerpt: 
```
recv chunk: b'{"id":123, "out':
recv chunk: b'put":"large_text\ncont'
recv chunk: b'..."}\n'
parser: waiting on more bytes, queue size -> 420
```
I'm using Python aiohttp streaming read and json.JSONDecoder(raw_decode) with a loop.

ashok: Two quick angles: 1) client incremental decode (codecs/JSONDecoder) + a small bounded queue + backpressure signal to processing task. 2) ask server to send whole JSON per event (server-side flush or send delim). Which is easier here?

marie: Server-side change is possible but risky for Dedicated customers. Prefer client fix first. Any compact code pointers?

kyle: Try this pattern: use codecs.getincrementaldecoder('utf-8') to safely reassemble multibyte chars across chunks, then feed bytes to a small stateful buffer and call json.JSONDecoder().raw_decode in a while loop. Also limit buffer length and drop/raise if over N to avoid memory blowup.

marie: Can you paste minimal snippet?

kyle: Sure — trimmed: 
```
decoder = codecs.getincrementaldecoder('utf-8')()
buf = ''
while True:
    chunk = await resp.content.read(1024)
    if not chunk: break
    s = decoder.decode(chunk)
    buf += s
    try:
        while buf:
            obj, idx = json.JSONDecoder().raw_decode(buf)
            handle(obj)
            buf = buf[idx:]
    except ValueError:
        # need more bytes
        if len(buf) > MAX_BUF:
            metrics.counter('sse.buf_overflow')
            buf = ''  # or raise
        continue
```

ashok: Also add a small asyncio.Queue(maxsize=200) between reader and handler so reader blocks on queue.put until consumer catches up — that creates backpressure at application level. If you can't block, drop oldest when full (depends on semantics).

tess: Useful: don't forget to set socket options (TCP_NODELAY) and disable Nagle if you control the server side — reduces coalescing that can split your event boundaries in odd ways. Also ensure server uses \r\n event delim or `event:` SSE framing properly.

marie: Good points. One oddity: some chunks are cutting multibyte UTF-8 sequences and my decoder was throwing. So getincrementaldecoder fixed that. After switching to bounded queue + incremental decoder buffer, memory spike stopped.

kyle: If you need ordering guarantees during retry, consider adding a lightweight header like `X-Chunk-Seq` or an event id per SSE event so reassembly is tolerant to retries.

marie: Will try sequence header and bounded queue. If I still see stalls I'll add an explicit heartbeat ack to let server drop/pause for slow consumers. Thanks! :thumbsup:

devex-bot: FYI — opened ticket DEVEX-5121 to capture recommended client patterns and add a Python example to docs.

marie: thanks, linking to repro PR once I have one.

marie: I'll take that. Ending for now.
